questions.solution: Correct Option B - Extra fascial hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO): The patient in the vignette above demonstrates complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. This process is secondary to thickening of the endometrial glands (typically due to unopposed oestrogen), and is considered a pre-cancerous lesion. Patients in this clinical situation that have completed childbearing should undergo a total extrafascial hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO). This recommendation is due to the relatively high probability of finding endometrial carcinoma during surgery. In addition, BSO is the standard of care in the treatment of endometrial carcinoma, and may spare the patient an additional surgical intervention. Incorrect Options: Option A - Extra Fascial Hysterectomy: While hysterectomy is a definitive treatment option, given the pathology result of complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia, there is a potential for progression to endometrial cancer. Therefore, more comprehensive management might be considered. Option C - Medroxyprogesterone Acetate (MPA): Hormone therapy with MPA might be considered as a conservative approach to manage certain cases of complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. However, the patient's post-menopausal status and the potential for malignancy make surgical intervention a more appropriate choice. Option D - Observation: Given the diagnosis of complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia, observation is generally not recommended. There is a potential for progression to endometrial cancer, and taking a more proactive approach to remove the source of the hyperplasia is often warranted. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a category 1 indication to perform plasma exchange plasmapheresis ?
questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is not a category 1 indication to perform plasma exchange plasmapheresis ?
questions.solution: Correct Option D - Shiga Toxin HUS: Shiga toxin-mediated hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) is not a Category 1 indication for plasma exchange. Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection leads to HUS, which primarily affects the kidneys and blood cells. Treatment mainly focuses on supportive care, hydration, and managing complications. Incorrect Options: Option A - Cryoglobulinemia: Cryoglobulinemia, especially with severe vasculitis, is a Category 1 indication for plasma exchange. This condition involves abnormal proteins that can precipitate at low temperatures and cause damage to blood vessels. Option B - Goodpasture Syndrome: Goodpasture syndrome, an autoimmune disorder affecting the lungs and kidneys, is a Category 1 indication for plasma exchange. It's aimed at removing circulating antibodies that attack these organs. Option C - Hyperviscosity Syndrome for Waldenstrom's: Hyperviscosity syndrome in Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia, a type of blood cancer, is also a Category 1 indication for plasma exchange. The procedure helps reduce the high levels of monoclonal IgM antibodies causing hyperviscosity. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: A 58-year-old male with refractory B-cell acute lymphoid leukemia (B-ALL, dx 6 months ago) is currently on ECOG 1910 regimen. He has atrial fibrillation on Lovenox and a history of pulmonary embolism. He is admitted to the ICU with acute neutropenic septic shock secondary to klebsiella bacteremia. There are no other associated symptoms like chest pain, cough, nausea, vomiting, rash, or headache. However, he reports 1-2 days of diarrhea. The decision is made to intubate due to an inability to compensate adequately for severe metabolic acidosis due to suspected gut translocation. Echocardiogram shows mildly dilated LA. LVEF is 60%. He has no valvular abnormalities and normal ventricular contractility. Chest X-ray shows increasing airspace opacities, bilateral lung bases, and midzone alveolar edema. Pneumonia is excluded. The patient has a persistent, small left pleural effusion with associated slight basal atelectasis. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is considered. As per the Berlin criteria, which oxygenation would label the ARDS as mild?

questions.solution: Correct Option A - 200 < PaO 2 /FiO 2 ≤ 300 with PEEP or CPAP ≥5cm H 2 O: The severity of ARDS is classified into 3 mutually exclusive categories of ARDS based on the degree of hypoxemia: mild (200 mmHg < PaO 2 /FIO 2 ≤ 300 mmHg), moderate (100 mmHg < PaO 2 /FIO 2 ≤ 200 mmHg), and severe (PaO 2 /FIO 2 ≤ 100 mmHg), all with PEEP or CPAP ≥5cm H 2 O. Using the Berlin definition, stages of mild, moderate, and severe ARDS are associated with increased mortality (27%; 95% CI, 24%-30%; 32%; 95% CI, 29%-34%; and 45%; 95% CI, 42%-48%, respectively; P <0.001) and increased median duration of mechanical ventilation in survivors (5 days; interquartile [IQR], 2-11; 7 days; IQR, 4-14; and 9 days; IQR, 5-17, respectively; P <0.001). Compared to the American-European Consensus Conference (AECC definition), the final Berlin definition had better predictive validity for mortality. Incorrect Options: Option B - 100 < PaO 2 /FiO 2 ≤ 200 with PEEP or CPAP ≥5cm H 2 O: This option corresponds to moderate ARDS (100 < PaO 2 /FiO 2 ≤ 200 with PEEP or CPAP ≥5cm H 2 O). questions.stem: A 37-year-old female presents to the ER with progressive shortness of breath and cough. At the time of presentation, she denies any systemic symptoms including weight loss, fever, chills, or night sweats. Laboratory evaluation at the time demonstrates profound normocytic and normochromic anaemia. Her WBC and platelets are within normal limits, as are her haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin and LDH. Her Coombs test is negative. What is the most likely explanation for this clinical presentation?
questions.stemHtml: A 37-year-old female presents to the ER with progressive shortness of breath and cough. At the time of presentation, she denies any systemic symptoms including weight loss, fever, chills, or night sweats. Laboratory evaluation at the time demonstrates profound normocytic and normochromic anaemia. Her WBC and platelets are within normal limits, as are her haptoglobin, indirect bilirubin and LDH. Her Coombs test is negative. What is the most likely explanation for this clinical presentation?
questions.solution: Correct Option B - Thymoma: In this scenario, the patient presents with progressive shortness of breath and cough along with profound normocytic and normochromic anemia. The laboratory results show a lack of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow, leading to pure red cell aplasia (PRCA). Thymoma is a tumor of the thymus gland, which is located in the mediastinum (the area between the lungs). Thymomas can be associated with paraneoplastic syndromes, and one of these syndromes is pure red cell aplasia (PRCA). PRCA is characterized by a significant reduction in reticulocytosis and erythroid precursors in the bone marrow, leading to profound anemia. Unlike aplastic anemia, other blood cell lines (white blood cells and platelets) are not usually affected. Thymomas can lead to PRCA through paraneoplastic mechanisms, where the tumor produces factors that interfere with normal hematopoiesis and erythropoiesis. Incorrect Options: Option A - Large Granular Lymphocytosis: Large granular lymphocytosis is a condition characterized by an increased number of large granular lymphocytes in the blood. It is not typically associated with profound normocytic and normochromic anemia. Option C - Anti-erythropoietin Antibodies: While anti-erythropoietin antibodies can interfere with erythropoiesis and lead to anemia, they are not a common cause of PRCA. Additionally, the presentation in the scenario does not align with this mechanism. Option D - Parvovirus B-19 Infection: Parvovirus B-19 infection can cause a temporary decrease in erythropoiesis, leading to anemia, but it usually affects individuals with underlying hemolytic conditions or compromised immune systems. The bone marrow aspiration finding mentioned (giant proerythroblasts) is characteristic of parvovirus B-19 infection but is not consistent with the described case. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: In reference to personality disorders, all of the following are accurate statements, EXCEPT?
questions.stemHtml: In reference to personality disorders, all of the following are accurate statements, EXCEPT?

options.label: A
options.text: These are disorders associated with enduring and ingrained behaviour patterns that deviate from that expected of an “average” individual

options.label: B
options.text: The behaviour should not be severe enough to lead to impaired functioning/performance in social, occupational and interpersonal domains

options.label: C
options.text: Individuals with personality disorders are more likely to seek out medical care

options.label: D
options.text: Patients with personality disorders have worse outcomes from comorbid medical or psychiatric conditions than individuals with the same conditions without comorbid personality disorders

questions.answerText: The behaviour should not be severe enough to lead to impaired functioning/performance in social, occupational and interpersonal domains
questions.solution: Correct Option B - The behaviour should not be severe enough to lead to impaired functioning/performance in social, occupational and interpersonal domains: All of the above statements are true except answer option B. A core, common element to all personality disorders is the presence of maladaptive behaviors that are ingrained or endure even though these behaviors result in stress or dysfunction in social and occupational environments. Patients with personality disorders are more likely to seek out medical care (e.g., an estimated 40% of patients in psychiatric practices by some studies), and are more likely to have worse outcomes from unrelated comorbid medical or psychiatric conditions, relative to patients with similar conditions without personality disorders. This finding is attributed to the poor coping skills and maladaptive behaviours (often self-harmful) common to this class of disorders. Incorrect Options: Option A - These are disorders associated with enduring and ingrained behaviour patterns that deviate from that expected of an "average" individual: This statement is accurate. Personality disorders involve enduring patterns of behaviour and thinking that deviate from societal norms and expectations. Individuals with personality disorders may seek medical care, often due to distress or impairment caused by their symptoms. Option D - Patients with personality disorders have worse outcomes from comorbid medical or psychiatric conditions than individuals with the same conditions without comorbid personality disorders: This statement is accurate. Comorbid personality disorders can complicate the course and treatment of other medical or psychiatric conditions. @Neet_pg_bot

This study included patients who resumed anticoagulation for comorbidities.
